answer: Cloned identities are blocked by a lantern registry tying each agent to one beacon-verified work record and one non-transferable stake. Admission needs a beacon response, a locked stake, and a peer audit. The k-th fake costs 20 plus 0.04 times k squared units: the registry enforces a quadratic cluster fee, the stake cannot be reused, and a failed audit forfeits the stake. One fake costs about 20 units; 1,000 cost 13,373,340. A device farm fails at the zenith cap on identities per cluster, as beacon checks expose one operator behind many names. An honest agent pays once.
